title: Solving Problems of Unknown Difficulty
abstract: arXiv:2604.00156v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper studies how uncertainty about problem difficulty shapes problem-solving strategies. I develop a dynamic model where an agent solves a problem by brainstorming approaches of unknown quality and allocating a fixed effort budget among them. Success arrives from spending effort pursuing good approaches, at a rate determined by the unknown problem difficulty. The agent balances costly exploration (expanding the set of approaches) with exploitation (pursuing existing approaches). Failures could signal either a bad idea or a hard problem, and this uncertainty generates novel dynamics: optimal search alternates between trying new approaches and revisiting previously abandoned ones. I then examine a principal-agent environment, where moral hazard arises on the intensive margin: how the agent explores. translated_abstract: 本文研究关于问题难度的不确定性如何塑造问题解决的策略。我构建了一个动态模型，其中代理人通过头脑风暴产生质量未知的方法，并在这些方法之间分配固定的努力预算。成功来自于在好的方法上投入努力，其成功速率由未知的问题难度决定。代理人需要在代价高昂的探索（扩展方法集合）与利用（追求已有方法）之间进行权衡。失败可能既意味着想法不好，也可能意味着问题很难，这种不确定性产生了新颖的动态特征：最优搜索会在尝试新方法与重新审视之前被放弃的方法之间交替进行。随后，我考察了一个委托-代理环境，其中道德风险出现在集约边际上：即代理人如何进行探索。动态承诺会产生一种前置力量，而学习机制的存在可以抵消这种力量。该框架反映了科学...
tldr: 本文构建了一个问题难度未知的动态求解模型，发现在无法区分失败源于“方法不佳”还是“问题困难”时，最优搜索会在尝试新方法与重新审视已放弃方法之间交替进行，并将其扩展到委托-代理环境中以分析探索行为上的道德风险问题。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a dynamic model of problem-solving under unknown difficulty, showing that when failures are ambiguous between signaling a bad idea or a hard problem, optimal search alternates between trying new approaches and revisiting abandoned ones, and extends the framework to a principal-agent setting with moral hazard in how the agent explores.
